title: Sindhu Lost to An Se Young Again. Ayush Shetty Fell After Winning the First Game. India's Singles Campaign at the Indonesia Open Is Over.
excerpt: Six Indian singles players entered the draw. All six are out by the second round. Only the doubles pairs remain in Jakarta.
body:
Six Indian singles players entered the Indonesia Open 2026 in Jakarta. PV Sindhu. Lakshya Sen. HS Prannoy. Kidambi Srikanth. Malvika Bansod. Ayush Shetty. By Thursday, all six were gone. Not one reached the quarterfinals.

The last two standing fell on the same day. Sindhu lost 17-21, 15-21 to world number one An Se Young of South Korea in 44 minutes. It was their tenth meeting. Sindhu has now lost all ten. Ayush Shetty, the 21-year-old who had pulled off a sensational comeback against China's Weng Hong Yang in the first round, lost 21-16, 13-21, 14-21 to Hong Kong's Lee Cheuk Yiu after winning the opening game.

For Sindhu, the pattern against An Se Young has become a weight. The Korean is simply the better player right now — more consistent in rallies, sharper in her court coverage, more clinical in converting advantages. Sindhu fought in the first game, staying within striking distance until 17-21. But the second game was more decisive. An Se Young pulled ahead 13-6 and never looked back.

## Ayush Shetty's Momentum Vanished

Shetty had been the feel-good story of India's Indonesia Open campaign. In the first round, he came back from 8-21 down in the opening game to defeat world number 15 Weng Hong Yang 8-21, 22-20, 21-15, winning three consecutive points from 19-20 down in the second game to force a decider. It was the kind of result that suggested a player finding his level on the biggest stage.

But against Lee Cheuk Yiu, the script flipped. Shetty won the first game 21-16 and appeared to be carrying forward his momentum from the previous round. Then something shifted. Lee took control in the second game, winning 21-13, and carried that dominance into the decider, winning 21-14. It was Shetty's third consecutive tournament without reaching the quarterfinals, a worrying run for a player who won an Asian Championships silver medal earlier this year.

## The First-Round Exits

The damage had been done before Thursday even arrived. Lakshya Sen, ranked 10th in the world and India's top-seeded men's singles player, lost in the first round. So did Kidambi Srikanth and HS Prannoy. On the women's side, Malvika Bansod was beaten by seventh seed Pornpawee Chochuwong 12-21, 10-21, and Unnati Hooda fell to Japan's Nozomi Okuhara 15-21, 14-21.

It was the kind of collective collapse that raises questions not about individual players but about the state of Indian badminton's singles depth below the very top tier. When six players enter a Super 1000 event and none reach the last eight, the conversation shifts from individual form to systemic gaps.

## What Remains

India still has representation in the doubles draws. The mixed doubles pair of Rohan Kapoor and Ruthvika Shivani upset the world number 20 pair in the first round, and Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were also in action. But the headline-grabbing entries — Sindhu, Lakshya, Prannoy — are all watching from the sidelines.

The withdrawal of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty with Satwik's recurring shoulder injury had already dimmed India's prospects earlier in the week. The pair had won the Singapore Open title just six days before Jakarta, but Satwik could not continue.

## The Bigger Question for NRI Fans

For diaspora fans who follow Indian badminton through tournament scores and YouTube highlights, the Indonesia Open tells a story they have been watching unfold for two years. Sindhu remains competitive but cannot break through against the very best. Lakshya and Prannoy have not produced consistent deep runs at the highest level. And the next generation — Shetty, Bansod, Hooda — are still learning what it takes to survive at Super 1000 events.

The next stop on the BWF World Tour is the Australian Open on June 9. The question is whether any of these results will change by then, or whether India's singles players will continue to exit early while the Asian powerhouses pull further ahead.
